lessons.title: Circle Time: Introduction to Body Awareness
lessons.content:
Learning Goal: Engage children with a physical rhyme to build auditory skills and basic body part recognition
.
Activity: Rhyme – Head, Shoulders, Knees, and Toes
.
Detailed Procedure: The teacher leads the students in singing the rhyme slowly, demonstrating how to touch the corresponding body parts (head, shoulders, knees, toes) as they are named. This builds gross motor skills and helps children follow physical cues.

lessons.title: Literacy: Introduction to Standing Line
lessons.content:
Learning Goal: Introduce the first pre-writing stroke, the vertical "Standing Line"
.
Concept: A standing line goes straight up and down.
Detailed Procedure & Activity: Demonstrate drawing a straight vertical line on the board. Then, transition to the English skillbook activity where students trace over the standing lines. The worksheet provides a visual of falling leaves from a tree, with dotted vertical lines descending from the leaves. Instruct students to trace from top to bottom
.

lessons.title: Numeracy: Introduction to Pre-Math Concept – Big and Small
lessons.content:
Learning Goal: Introduce size differentiation and comparison
.
Concept: Understanding the visual difference between large (big) and small objects.
Detailed Procedure: Use classroom objects (like a large book and a small book) to demonstrate the concept visually. Emphasize the vocabulary "Big" and "Small" clearly so students begin associating the words with the physical scale.

lessons.title: General Awareness (EVS): Introduction to "All About Me"
lessons.content:
Learning Goal: Encourage self-recognition and personal identity
.
Concept: Knowing basic personal facts.
Detailed Procedure & Activity: Conduct an oral session asking simple questions such as "What is your name?" and "What is your age?"
. Encourage each child to speak loudly and confidently.

lessons.title: Circle Time: Revisit Rhyme
lessons.content:
Activity: Revisit – Head, Shoulders, Knees, and Toes
.
Detailed Procedure: Sing the rhyme again, this time increasing the speed slightly to make it a fun, energetic physical activity that tests their recall and coordination.

lessons.title: Literacy: Revisit Standing Line
lessons.content:
Activity: Revisit – Standing Line
.
Detailed Procedure: Continue practicing the vertical stroke. Ensure students are holding their crayons correctly and tracing the dotted lines downwards to build muscle memory
.

lessons.title: Numeracy: Revisit Big and Small
lessons.content:
Activity: Revisit – Big and Small
.
Detailed Procedure & Activity: Move to the Maths skillbook application. Guide students through the visual discrimination tasks. Instruct them to "Circle the big objects" (using examples from the book like the big box and the large teddy bear) and "Circle the small objects" (like the small soccer ball and the small blue hat)
.

lessons.title: General Awareness (EVS): Revisit All About Me
lessons.content:
Activity: Revisit – All About Me
.
Detailed Procedure & Activity: Expand on self-identity by discussing their personal preferences. Ask oral questions like "Name your favourite toy"
. This encourages children to express their individual likes within a group setting.

lessons.title: Circle Time: Introduction to Story
lessons.content:
Learning Goal: Introduce narrative listening, attention span, and moral comprehension
.
Activity: Intro – Story: The Tortoise and the Rabbit
.
Detailed Procedure: Read the story aloud to the class. Introduce the two main characters (the slow tortoise and the fast rabbit) and describe the setting of the race.

lessons.title: Literacy: Introduction to Sleeping Line
lessons.content:
Learning Goal: Introduce the horizontal pre-writing stroke
.
Concept: A sleeping line goes across from left to right.
Detailed Procedure & Activity: Demonstrate the horizontal stroke. In the English skillbook, have students trace over the sleeping lines. This activity uses fun associations, asking children to trace the dotted horizontal line to connect animals to their homes: linking the bee to the beehive, the lion to the den, and the dog to the kennel
.

lessons.title: Numeracy: Revisit Big and Small
lessons.content:
Activity: Revisit – Big and Small
.
Detailed Procedure: Continue assessing their grasp of size. Use oral questioning and point-and-identify methods, asking students to "Point to the big object" when shown contrasting images (e.g., a big teddy bear next to a small one)
.

lessons.title: General Awareness (EVS): Introduction to Genders
lessons.content:
Learning Goal: Identify biological gender categories
.
Concept: Differentiating between a boy and a girl.
Detailed Procedure & Activity: Ask the children, "Are you a boy or a girl?"
. Follow up with a worksheet activity where students look at pictures of children and "Tick (✔) below" the image that matches their own gender (a picture of a girl reading, or a boy with a backpack)
.

lessons.title: Circle Time: Revisit Story
lessons.content:
Activity: Revisit – The Tortoise and the Rabbit
.
Detailed Procedure: Recap the plot of the story. Discuss the ending and the moral lesson of the story, emphasizing that taking your time and not giving up is better than rushing and being careless.

lessons.title: Literacy: Revisit Sleeping Line
lessons.content:
Activity: Revisit – Sleeping Line
.
Detailed Procedure & Activity: Continue the matching activity from Day 3, tracing horizontal lines from left to right. Have them connect the bird to the nest, the horse to the stable, and the girl to the house
. Focus on keeping the crayon on the dotted line.

lessons.title: Numeracy: Revisit Big and Small
lessons.content:
Activity: Revisit – Big and Small
.
Detailed Procedure: Consolidate the size concept through a physical classroom activity. Ask students to sort mixed items (like blocks or toy cars) into a "Big" pile and a "Small" pile.

lessons.title: General Awareness (EVS): Revisit Genders
lessons.content:
Activity: Revisit – Genders
.
Detailed Procedure: Further discuss differences and similarities between boys and girls. You can use visual aids of clothing items (like a skirt, dress, shirt, and shorts) to discuss different types of clothes children wear
.

lessons.title: Circle Time: Synthesis
lessons.content:
Activity: Revisit – Rhyme and Story
.
Detailed Procedure: Have a final, enthusiastic group performance of the Head, Shoulders, Knees, and Toes rhyme. Ask students to recall their favourite part of The Tortoise and the Rabbit.

lessons.title: Literacy: Revisit Standing and Sleeping Line
lessons.content:
Activity: Revisit – Standing and Sleeping Line
.
Detailed Procedure: Combine both strokes. Have children practice drawing a simple shape, like a window or a ladder, which requires them to use both top-to-bottom (standing) and left-to-right (sleeping) motions.

lessons.title: Numeracy: Revisit Big and Small - Activity
lessons.content:
Activity: Revisit – Big and Small - Activity
.
Detailed Procedure: Conduct a final review activity, perhaps pointing out big and small objects around the actual classroom (e.g., the big teacher's desk vs. a small chair).

lessons.title: General Awareness (EVS): Revisit All About Me, and Genders
lessons.content:
Activity: Revisit – All about me, and Genders
.
Detailed Procedure: Bring the week's themes together by having children introduce themselves to the class: "My name is [Name], I am [Age] years old, and I am a [Boy/Girl]".

lessons.title: Art and Craft: Hand Painting
lessons.content:
Learning Goal: Sensory engagement and introduction to primary colours
.
Activity: Activity – Hand Painting
.
Detailed Procedure: Introduce the Primary Colour RED
. Instruct the children to "Paint your hand red and make a palm print" on their art pages
. This messy, fun activity develops tactile senses while solidifying colour recognition.

lessons.title: All About Me
lessons.content: Learning Goal: To encourage self-recognition, express individual preferences, and state basic personal facts. Activity: Oral introduction and gender identification worksheet. Detailed procedure: Conduct an oral session asking simple questions such as 'What is your name?', 'What is your age?', and 'Name your favourite toy.' Ask the children 'Are you a boy or a girl?' and provide a written activity where students look at pictures of a boy and a girl and tick the image that matches their own gender.

lessons.title: My Body Parts
lessons.content: Learning Goal: To identify, name, and understand that each part of our body is important. Activity: Oral naming and body part matching. Detailed procedure: Show flashcards or point to different body parts and ask the child to orally name the given parts of the body. Provide a worksheet featuring a picture of a child and ask students to match the body parts by drawing lines from isolated images of a hand, leg, and foot to the correct location on the child's body

lessons.title: Body Parts
lessons.content: Learning Goal: To visually distinguish specific upper and lower limbs from other objects. Activity: Circling body parts among distractors. Detailed procedure: Give students a mixed group of pictures containing items like an apple, a banana, a hand, and a foot. Instruct the children to circle only the body parts to assess their visual discrimination. Focus on body vocabulary such as Shoulder, Elbow, Wrist, Thumb, Fingers, Thigh, Knee, Foot, Heel, and Toes

lessons.title: Face parts
lessons.content: Learning Goal: To isolate and identify specific sensory organs and features located on the face. Activity: Identification game and facial feature matching. Detailed procedure: Point to facial features and ask the child to orally name the given parts of the body, specifically focusing on the ear, eye, and nose. Follow up with a matching activity where students draw a line from an isolated picture of an ear, eye, or nose to the corresponding correct place on the pictured boy's face

lessons.title: All About Me
lessons.content: Learning Goal: To consolidate foundational concepts of personal identity, gender, and family information. Activity: Name and age presentation and family member identification. Detailed procedure: Have the children confidently state their name and age as a review of their personal identity. Revisit the core oral questions like 'Are you a boy or a girl?' and 'Name 2 members of your family.' Provide a worksheet asking students to tick the family members that are part of their family to reinforce their personal context

lessons.title: My Body Parts

Detailed procedure: Show flashcards or point to different body parts and ask the child to orally name the given parts of the body. Provide a worksheet featuring a picture of a child and ask students to match the body parts by drawing lines from isolated images of a hand, leg, and foot to the correct location on the child's body

Detailed procedure: Point to facial features and ask the child to orally name the given parts of the body, specifically focusing on the ear, eye, and nose. Follow up with a matching activity where students draw a line from an isolated picture of an ear, eye, or nose to the corresponding correct place on the pictured boy's face

lessons.title: Head, Shoulders, Knees, Toes
lessons.content: Learning Goal: To build auditory skills, introduce body part recognition, and develop gross motor coordination. Activity: Rhyme introduction and physical movement. Detailed procedure: The teacher leads the students in singing the rhyme 'Head, Shoulders, Knees, and Toes' slowly. As each body part is named, the teacher demonstrates touching the corresponding area (head, shoulders, knees, toes), encouraging the children to follow along and physically engage with the song to build physical vocabulary connections.

lessons.title: Big and Small
lessons.content: Learning Goal: To introduce size differentiation and comparison vocabulary, helping children visually distinguish between large and small objects. Activity: Visual demonstration using pictures or real-life objects. Detailed procedure: Use contrasting images or items, such as a big gift box and a small gift box, or a big dog and a small dog. Emphasize the vocabulary 'Big' and 'Small' clearly as you point to each object, so students begin associating the words with physical scale

lessons.title: Standing lines
lessons.content: Learning Goal: To introduce the first pre-writing stroke, the vertical standing line, to build foundational fine motor skills and hand-eye coordination. Activity: Vertical tracing practice. Detailed procedure: Demonstrate drawing a straight vertical line on the board. Then, instruct students to use their skillbook to trace over the dotted standing lines descending from the leaves, focusing on maintaining a steady grip from top to bottom.

lessons.title: All About Me

Detailed procedure: Conduct an oral session asking simple questions such as 'What is your name?', 'What is your age?', and 'Name your favourite toy.' Ask the children 'Are you a boy or a girl?' and provide a written activity where students look at pictures of a boy and a girl and tick the image that matches their own gender.
